overview: TechnologyOne is an Australian-founded, ASX-listed enterprise software company that develops, markets, sells, implements, and supports a fully integrated SaaS ERP suite (finance, HR/payroll, asset management, student management, property/rating, and more) for government, local government, higher education, and health/community sector customers. The company operates primarily in Australia and New Zealand (APAC, ~82-83% of revenue), with a fast-growing UK operation (~9% of ARR) and a small Solomon Islands/Pacific presence. Over the past decade it has transitioned its ~1,250+ customer base from on-premise licenses to a single-instance, multi-tenanted SaaS model, and since 2023 has pioneered 'SaaS+' - a one-fee, rapid-implementation model that bundles software and implementation together.

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated from SaaS/recurring subscription fees (the large majority of revenue), consulting/implementation services, and a small corporate/other category. The SaaS+ model has shifted lower-quality, one-off consulting revenue into higher-quality, long-term recurring SaaS fees, lifting new-deal ARR value by roughly 40%. Approximately 90%+ of total revenue is now SaaS and recurring in nature, with Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) of $554.6m (FY2025) representing 91% of total revenue and growing toward a $1bn+ ARR target by FY30.
business_model.customer_type: B2G/B2B - government agencies, local councils, higher education institutions, health and community service providers, and asset/project-intensive and corporate/financial services organisations; over 1,250 customer organisations
business_model.geographic_mix: APAC (Australia, New Zealand, Pacific) ~82.5% of profit/ARR, United Kingdom ~9.3% and growing fastest (UK ARR up 49% in FY25, up 23% YoY in H1 FY26), New Zealand ~8.2%

competitive_position.market_position: Dominant/leading position in Australian and New Zealand local government ERP (self-reported ~73% of the APAC population lives in councils using TechnologyOne solutions) and a top SaaS provider for Higher Education in Australia, New Zealand and the UK; a smaller but rapidly growing challenger to incumbents (Civica, Capita) in UK local government and higher education.

moat_factors.description: ERP systems run core finance, HR/payroll, asset and citizen-service workflows; 99% customer retention and ~1% annual churn reflect how costly and risky it is for customers to replace the system once implemented

20 licensable products and 500+ modules built specifically for six vertical markets (government, local government, education, health, asset-intensive industries, corporates/financial services), with deep compliance/regulatory functionality (e.g., payroll award interpretation, data sovereignty) that generic global ERP vendors do not match for these niches

Combining ERP software and implementation into one fee materially de-risks and speeds up deployment (target: ERP in 30 days by 2028, down from ~300 days historically) versus traditional multi-year, multi-vendor consulting-led implementations from SAP/Oracle/Big 4 integrators

Invests 20-25% of revenue in R&D ($153.7m in FY25, up 20%), funding the largest commercial R&D centre of its kind in Australia plus offshore facilities in Indonesia and Vietnam; enables continuous product evolution (AI-enabled 'Plus' product, 20th product launched FY25) versus smaller niche vendors

Single data lake across the ERP suite is positioned as the foundation for agentic AI features (Plus), which management argues increases switching costs further as customers adopt more AI-driven workflows across more products
38-year track record, AFR Customer Champion Leader 2025, high customer NPS/referenceability driving sales, particularly cited as a key factor in winning UK council and university tenders

weaknesses: Heavy geographic concentration in Australia/NZ (~82-91% of ARR/profit) limits diversification; UK and other international expansion is still a small share of the business despite fast growth
Narrow sector focus (public sector, education, health) makes growth dependent on government budgets and public-sector IT spending cycles
Small scale globally relative to SAP, Oracle, Workday and Microsoft, which have vastly larger R&D budgets, broader product suites and global sales forces

Premium valuation historically vulnerable to sharp de-ratings on even modest ARR/NRR misses (e.g., ~17% single-day share price fall in November 2025 on a softer-than-expected ARR/NRR print despite a record result)
Limited public security/SLA benchmarking versus larger global competitors, per some independent reviews

growth_drivers: Continued migration of remaining on-premise/legacy customers to SaaS and then to SaaS+, with SaaS+ lifting ARR value per deal by ~40%

UK expansion - UK ARR up 49% in FY25 and up 23% YoY in H1 FY26, driven by local government and higher education wins (Royal Borough of Greenwich, Islington, University of Hertfordshire, Royal Holloway), with a long-term goal of UK council amalgamation creating larger tender opportunities

Whitespace within the existing APAC customer base - management states current penetration of any single vertical does not exceed ~15% of addressable market, implying significant room for cross-sell/up-sell of additional products and modules (average ARR per customer has grown from $100k in FY12 to >$440k in FY25 and >$491k in H1 FY26)

New product launches - Plus (agentic AI product, 20th product, launched February 2026) and 'Guide', DxP (Digital Experience Platform), App Builder, and ERP in 30 Days initiative (targeting 30-day implementations by 2028, down from ~300 days historically)
AI-driven, transaction-based ARR uplift - management has flagged a new AI transaction-driven ARR strategy as an additional lever toward the $1bn+ ARR by FY30 target

Inorganic growth via bolt-on, IP-related M&A (CourseLoop acquisition completed November 2024 for ~$60m, expected EPS-accretive from FY26) funded from a debt-free balance sheet with ~$320m (FY25) to $245m (H1 FY26) of cash and investments
Operating leverage / margin expansion - management guides to Profit Before Tax margin expanding to 35%+ over the medium term (from 30% in FY25) as SaaS+ economies of scale are realised
Secular public-sector digital transformation and replacement of ageing legacy government/education systems with cloud ERP

business.description: FY25 ARR growth (18%) missed consensus by ~2 points and NRR eased to 115% (from 117% FY24, 114% H1 FY26); given the market's heavy reliance on ARR as the primary valuation driver, any further deceleration could trigger sharp re-ratings as seen in November 2025

business.risk: Customer concentration in government/public sector budgets
business.description: Government, local government and education customers are subject to budget cycles, elections, and fiscal constraints that can delay procurement decisions and implementations

business.risk: Competitive displacement risk in core verticals
business.description: Global ERP vendors (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Workday) and specialist local competitors (Civica, Capita) compete for the same tenders; while TechnologyOne cites competitive win-backs (e.g., City of Townsville returning after trying a competitor), losses to or defections toward competitors remain a risk, particularly in the UK where incumbents are entrenched

business.risk: Execution risk on AI strategy and new products
business.description: Plus and Guide are newly launched (Plus available Feb 2026); customer adoption curves, pricing realization and whether AI features translate into incremental ARR (rather than being bundled for free) are unproven at scale
Reliance on CEO Edward Chung and senior leadership team's continuity of strategy; founder Adrian Di Marco has progressively exited the business and sold down his shareholding over recent years

financial.description: As UK ARR becomes a larger share of the business (now ~9% and growing fastest), GBP/AUD translation volatility will have a growing effect on reported results

Roughly 55% of R&D spend is capitalised (not expensed) under the company's accounting policy; this is consistent with SaaS peer practice but means reported profit margins benefit from capitalisation choices that a reader must adjust for when comparing to fully-expensed peers

financial.risk: Rising payout ratio reduces reinvestment buffer
financial.description: Dividend payout ratio was lifted to 65-75% from FY26 (from 55-65%), and FY25's total payout ratio (including the special dividend) reached 87% of NPAT; while the balance sheet remains debt-free with strong cash generation, a structurally higher payout ratio leaves less flexibility if cash flow timing (traditionally weighted to H2) disappoints

regulatory.description: As a provider of mission-critical software to government and health customers, TechnologyOne must maintain extensive security accreditations (achieved ISO 42001:2023 for AI management systems in FY25); failure to maintain these or a security incident could be reputationally and commercially damaging given the sensitivity of government/citizen data

Emerging AI regulation in Australia, UK and elsewhere (particularly around public-sector use of agentic AI) could affect the pace of customer adoption of Plus/Guide or impose additional compliance costs

Changes in government IT procurement frameworks (e.g., panel arrangements, preference for sovereign/local vendors) could cut both ways - the recent Australian Energy Regulator federal government win under the Digital Transformation Agency panel is a positive example, but policy shifts could also favor or disadvantage TechnologyOne versus global rivals

macro.description: TNE has historically traded at a high earnings multiple reflecting its SaaS growth profile; broader shifts in risk appetite for high-multiple growth/tech stocks (e.g., tech sector-wide de-ratings noted by brokers in November 2025) can compress the multiple independent of company fundamentals
As a long-duration growth stock with cash flows weighted to future years, TNE's valuation is sensitive to changes in risk-free rates and equity discount rates

macro.risk: Public sector spending cycles / fiscal tightening
macro.description: Government austerity or fiscal consolidation in Australia, NZ or the UK could slow new contract wins or delay module upsells, though TechnologyOne's products are often pitched as delivering cost savings (customers report savings of 40%+) which can be a defensive positioning in tighter budget environments

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global enterprise SaaS/ERP spending continues to grow as organisations migrate from on-premise and legacy systems to cloud; public sector and education verticals are considered a large underpenetrated opportunity, with TechnologyOne citing a AU$13.5bn total addressable market across its core verticals and geographies
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate - government, local government, health and education customers have relatively stable, non-discretionary IT budgets compared to commercial enterprises, giving the business a degree of defensiveness; however, new contract wins and upsell can be delayed by budget cycles and elections
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirect sensitivity via its growth-stock valuation multiple, despite having no debt and a net cash balance sheet
key_input_costs: Skilled software engineering/R&D talent (Australia, Indonesia, Vietnam)
Sales, marketing and Showcase event investment

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 results: record first-half Profit Before Tax of $89.1m (up 9%, 28% margin), ARR of $598.0m (up 17% YoY), NRR of 114%, UK ARR up 23% to $53.0m, interim dividend up 21% to 8.0 cps; management reaffirmed confidence in hitting the top of FY26 ARR growth guidance (16-18%) given growth is historically weighted to H2

Mixed broker actions through the year: UBS downgraded to Hold (~$32 target, April 2026); Bell Potter moved from Buy to Hold in April 2026 citing valuation after a share price rally, then raised target/multiples in June while still seeing limited upside; Jarden upgraded to Overweight ($31 target) in May 2026; Morgan Stanley maintained Overweight (~$32 target); Canaccord Genuity cut its target sharply (from ~$44.82 to $32.00) post-FY25 result while maintaining Overweight

TechnologyOne upgraded FY26 guidance: Profit Before Tax growth raised to 18-20% (from 13-17%) and ARR growth guidance of 16-18%, citing strong SaaS+ momentum and AI-enhanced product uptake; company targeting the top end of both ranges

Launch of 'Plus', TechnologyOne's 20th product - an enterprise-wide agentic AI system built on the company's data lake, available from February 2026, designed to work across the whole product suite via natural-language interaction

FY2025 full-year results released: record revenue of $610.0m (up 18%), PBT of $181.5m (up 19%, beating prior guidance of 13-17%), NPAT of $137.6m (up 17%), ARR of $554.6m (up 18%), total dividend of 36.6 cps (up 63%, including a 10 cps special dividend), Rule of 40 of 59% (up from 52%). Despite the record result, shares fell ~17% on the day as ARR/NRR growth missed consensus by roughly 2 percentage points and brokers flagged slowing growth, rising costs (Showcase/AI investment) and valuation concerns

AI strategy formally launched at the company's Showcase event (new fifth-generation, agentic-AI-enabled ERP platform), with elevated marketing/event spend in H1 FY26 ($8-9m) weighing on near-term margins but positioned as a long-term growth catalyst

Continued UK momentum - won London Borough of Islington and Royal Borough of Greenwich (local government), University of Hertfordshire, Royal Holloway, University of Suffolk (higher education); City of Townsville in Australia returned to TechnologyOne after a failed attempt with a competitor, signing a 10-year SaaS+ deal worth 3x its prior contract value
Completed acquisition of CourseLoop (~$60m) for curriculum management IP, strengthening the Higher Education product suite; expected EPS-accretive from FY26

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 results (18 May 2026), reaffirming February 2026 upgraded guidance

items.notes: Raised from the original FY26 guidance of 13-17% given at the FY25 result (Nov 2025); management is targeting the top of the range. H1 FY26 PBT grew only 9% due to ~$8-9m of AI/Showcase launch costs, but management says growth excluding Showcase was ~19% and is weighted to H2
H1 FY26 ARR of $598.0m was up 17% YoY; management says strong H1 performance positions the company to hit the top of the range, supported by growth historically being H2-weighted
H1 FY26 NRR was 114%, slightly below the target range; FY25 NRR was 115% (down from 117% in FY24)

items.target: Above 40% (targeting top quartile of global SaaS peers)
items.notes: FY25 achieved 59% (up from 52% FY24); H1 FY26 Rule of 40 was 55%
New long-term target announced at FY25 results, raised after surpassing the prior $500m ARR target 18 months ahead of schedule (achieved in H1 FY25); current ARR base is $598.0m (H1 FY26)
FY25 PBT margin was 30% (flat vs FY24); management expects a temporary headwind from SaaS+/AI investment (~2.7pts impact in FY25) to reverse into a long-term tailwind as scale economies are realised
FY25 R&D investment was $153.7m (25% of total revenue, up 20% YoY); H1 FY26 R&D investment was $84.1m (26% of total income, up 22% YoY), ~54% capitalised
Raised from 55-65% (policy set FY24); FY25 payout ratio was 63% before the special dividend (87% including it); H1 FY26 interim dividend was 8.0 cps, up 21% YoY

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Edward Chung has emphasized that 'SaaS+ and our products turbocharged through AI are our not-so-secret weapons,' framing FY26 as a pivotal year with the launch of the agentic-AI-enabled Plus product. Management has repeatedly stressed that revenue and cash flow are structurally weighted to the second half (due to customer anniversary billing dates), so H1 results (9% PBT growth, 55% Rule of 40) understate full-year momentum; underlying PBT growth excluding one-off Showcase/AI launch costs was characterized as ~19%. The Board reiterated confidence in reaching $1bn+ ARR by FY30 and 35%+ PBT margins over the medium term, while acknowledging 'the economic outlook and geopolitical issues continue to create uncertainty.'

bull_case: Industry-leading SaaS economics - 99% customer retention, ~1% annual churn, 115%+ net revenue retention, and a Rule of 40 result of 59% (FY25) place TechnologyOne in the top quartile of global SaaS businesses, evidencing a durable moat in its core verticals

SaaS+ model structurally improves revenue quality and deal economics (lifting new ARR value ~40%) while shortening implementation times toward a goal of 'ERP in 30 days,' which should support both growth and eventual margin expansion to 35%+

Large, credible growth runway: management cites <15% penetration of APAC whitespace within its existing customer base, a $13.5bn total addressable market, and a newly raised $1bn+ ARR by FY30 target (after beating the prior $500m target 18 months early)

UK is a genuine second growth engine, with ARR up 49% in FY25 and 23% YoY in H1 FY26, driven by competitive wins against entrenched incumbents (Civica, Capita) in local government and higher education

Debt-free balance sheet with strong, growing free cash flow (FCF to NPAT ratio of 134% in FY25) funds both a rising dividend (payout ratio lifted to 65-75%) and optionality for further bolt-on, IP-accretive M&A like CourseLoop
bear_case: Premium valuation leaves little room for error - the ~17% single-day share price fall in November 2025 on a record result but a modest ARR/NRR miss shows how sensitive the stock is to any deceleration in its key SaaS metrics

Growth is becoming harder to sustain off a larger ARR base ($554.6m-$598m); FY25 ARR growth missed consensus, and NRR has drifted down from 117% (FY24) to 114% (H1 FY26), nearer the bottom of its 115-120% target range

Heavy geographic and vertical concentration (APAC public sector/education ~82-91% of the business) leaves the company exposed to government budget cycles and policy shifts, with international diversification (UK) still a small share of the total despite rapid growth

AI/Plus strategy and associated cost increases (e.g., Showcase event spend, elevated marketing) are unproven at scale - it remains to be seen whether agentic AI features translate into monetizable, incremental ARR or are simply bundled into existing contracts, while near-term margin guidance (35%+ medium-term vs 30% today) requires sustained execution

Broker sentiment has turned more cautious through 2026 (Bell Potter downgrade to Hold, UBS Hold, some target cuts), reflecting concern that the stock's high multiple already prices in continued best-in-class execution, leaving limited margin of safety if growth normalises
